units.translation: 6 with the rest changed, P adds the common etymology: λέγεται δὲ οὕτως ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴειν τὸ κομίζειν· κομιστικὰ γὰρ τὰ πηδάλια
b. 〈ἔρυσθαι:〉 to guard. Lg
402a. 〈λάιγγας:〉 stones. Lg
b. 〈ὀχλίζοντες:〉 moving. Lg
403a. νήεον αὐτόθ〈ι〉: they were building, constructing, from the placing together of stones, which is νῆσις. Or they were heaping up; hence also ναῦς, in which the cargo is heaped up.

2 379. Et. Gen. (AB) πήχυιον: such as I 379... | 11 ναῦς: Et. Or. 107, 11 | Et. M. 598, 18 | Eust. 741, 60. 1487, 4 | νηδύς: Et. Αἱμ. 627, 9 | Et. Or. 107, 32 | Et. M. 603, 4. 605, 1 | Et. Gud. 407, 15. 28. 31 Sturz | Epim. Cram. An. Ox. II 395, 8
11 νῆσις in W : νήησις | ναῦς in L : νηδύς in P : νηδὺς καὶ ναῦς in F
b. 〈νηόν:〉 it is written βωμόν. Gg
c. ἐπάκτιος is the one honored on the shore. Lm(P)

406. τείως δ’ αὖτ’ ἀγέλη〈θεν ἐπιπροέηκαν:〉 in the meantime, while they were doing these things. The preposition πρό here indicates place, meaning "forward," as in "ἐκ δ’ ἄγαγε πρὸ φόωσδε" (Iliad 19.118).
15 added by W
407. δύω βόε: reasonably, for the two titles "Ἀκτίου Ἐμβασίου τε" (v. 404) they bring two oxen.

408. κουρότεροι: since perhaps the god is always young, and the younger of the companions perform the sacrifice. Homer also, in the sacrifice of the young men (Iliad 1.470): "κοῦροι μὲν κρητῆρας ἐπεστέψαντο". So it is either comparative or in the positive degree. L
409. οὐλοχύτας: some say the baskets, because through them the sacrificial materials are carried; others say the barley grains, because they threw them whole on the altars.
1 sch. ABT A 449 | Apoll. Lex. Hom. 124, 15 B. | Hesych. οὐλ. | Eust. 132, 22. 38. 133, 18
1 οὐλοχύτας in W : χέρνιβα οἱ μὲν — βωμοῖς in L : χέρνιβα μέν... οὐλοχύτας δέ... in P. cf. W 41
411. Αἰσωνίδ〈α〉: Aesonis is a city of Magnesia named after Jason's father, as Pindar (fr. 273 Schr.) and Pherecydes (3 fr. 103a J.) say.
3 Steph. Byz. Αἰσών
413. ἄνυσιν καὶ πείραθ’ ὁδ〈οῖο〉: ἄνυσιν means the accomplishment. Homer (Iliad 4.56): "οὐκ ἀνύω φθονέουσα". πείραθ’ ὁδοῖο means the voyage itself and the end of the journey.
6 ἢ τὴν ταχυτῆτα added after ἐνέργειαν by P | 7 the words Ὅμηρος — φθονέουσα... restored by F
414. ἐπαίτιοε: because he prophesied to Pelias. Rhetorically, as if the god were responsible for the voyage, he attributes the whole affair to him as his own.
9 ἐπαίτιος — Πελίᾳ in L : τὸ δὲ ἐπαίτιος ἢ πρὸς τὸ δοθὲν μάντευμα... in P (cf. W 38)
416. παλίνορσον ἐς Ἑλλά〈δα〉: Some say Hellas is Phthia, using the name synonymously, but we understand Hellas to be a region, not the same as Phthia.
16 τῷ α' τών in L : γ' in P
